channel.title: Entuned Blog | Retail Music Strategy
channel.description: Research-backed insights on retail music strategy, in-store customer behavior, and AI-powered audio optimization.

item.title: Every Store Is About to Sound Different
item.description: Music is following scent design's path from generic catalog to designed brand layer. Early movers compound outcome data late adopters can't replicate.

item.title: What If You Licensed Music the Way Film and TV Do?
item.description: Sync licensing gives film and TV music chosen for the scene. Retail can't afford it. Composition delivers intentional fit at retail economics.

item.title: You're Licensing Technology That Doesn't Work
item.description: Retailers license music services that fail the basic technology test. The IP works fine. It just wasn't built to do the job your store actually needs done.

item.title: Madonna Never Got Your Design Brief
item.description: Every layer of your store gets a design brief. The music doesn't. Retailers borrow songs composed for concerts and movies, then wonder why the floor feels off.

item.title: The Most Expensive Paperweight in Your Store
item.description: Music shifts what shoppers buy, how long they stay, and how much they spend. Most stores still treat it as decor. Here is what the research shows.

item.title: One Playlist for Everyone Is a Playlist for No One
item.description: Picking a mood from a dropdown is selecting from a menu, not designing. Specificity is where retail music value lives, and playlists can't do specificity.

item.title: The Most Expensive Air in Retail
item.description: Every retail variable gets designed except one. The music in the air carries ideas written for someone else's purpose into the heads of every shopper in the room.

item.title: She Said Exactly What the Music Told Her to Say
item.description: A customer at our UNTUCKit pilot repeated an Entuned song lyric back as her buying decision without knowing it. This is semantic priming through music.

item.title: The Invisible Obvious, Part 1: Hands
item.description: Why doctors in 1847 refused to wash their hands, and what it took to change. Part 1 of a 5-part series about variables hiding in plain sight.

item.title: The Invisible Obvious, Part 2: Letters
item.description: In 2012, Errol Morris ran a typography experiment in the NYT. Forty thousand readers saw the same passage in different fonts, and Baskerville changed belief.

item.title: The Invisible Obvious, Part 3: Bodies
item.description: Body language was treated as too soft for serious research for most of the twentieth century, until trial lawyers and sales teams started using it.

item.title: The Invisible Obvious, Part 4: Light
item.description: Retail lighting was infrastructure until researchers started measuring what color temperature, brightness, and directionality were doing to spending.

item.title: The Invisible Obvious, Part 5: Sound
item.description: Music in retail is where lighting was in 1985. Four decades of research show tempo, mode, and genre shift purchasing. The technology to act on it now exists.

item.title: 127 BPM in a Target on a Tuesday
item.description: Most stores have no spec for the tempo of their background music. Here's what that costs in dwell time and basket size, backed by four decades of research.

item.title: Free and Legal Music for Retail Stores: Every Option for Playing Music Without PRO Fees
item.description: A complete guide to playing music legally in your retail store, from PRO licenses to commercial streaming services to free alternatives that eliminate music licensing fees entirely.

item.title: Music Licensing Compliance: A Hidden Liability Risk for Commercial Landlords and Property Managers
item.description: Your retail tenants are probably playing unlicensed music right now. Here's why that's a problem for your lease, your vacancy rate, and possibly your own legal exposure.

item.title: Music Licensing for Retail Stores: Fines, Lawsuits, and What Every Store Owner Should Know
item.description: Most retail stores play music without the right license. Here's what the law actually says, what the fines look like, and why your personal Spotify account doesn't cover commercial use.

item.title: Retail Music Has a Quality Problem
item.description: Carefully designed retail spaces are piping low-fidelity, cheaply licensed music through their speakers. The reason is structural, not aesthetic.

item.title: You Didn't Notice the Music. That's the Point.
item.description: If you ran a shift on Entuned and didn't really notice the music, that's the system working. Retail music is environmental design — judged by what moves, not what gets noticed.

item.title: What Is AI Music for Retail Stores?
item.description: A definitive read on AI music for retail stores in 2026. What it is, what it actually does, what it costs, and how it differs from licensed catalog music.
